records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל־צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל־מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: Listen to me, pursuers of righteousness, seekers of Yahweh: look to [the] rock [from which] you were hewn, and to [the] excavation of [the] pit [from which] you were dug out.
pieces: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who chase after righteousness, you who seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q look to the rock you were cut from, \q to the hollow of the pit you were dug out of.

L.1: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [you] pursuers of righteousness, seekers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q look to the rock [from which] you were hewn, \q and to the quarry of the pit [from which] you were dug.

R.1: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who want to do what is right and who turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Think about where you came from. \q You are like stone that was cut from a great rock, dug out of a deep quarry.

decisions.choice: the rock you were hewn from, the quarry you were dug from: the ancestors the people came from
decisions.reason: Verse 2 explains the picture: the rock and the quarry are Abraham and Sarah. As stone is cut from a quarry, the nation was cut from them.

decisions.choice: pursuers of righteousness: those who earnestly seek to live rightly, and to see God set things right
decisions.reason: Righteousness here is both right living and the right order God promises to bring (verses 5-8; Deuteronomy 16:20). The hearers are the faithful in Israel, who also "seek the LORD".

decisions.choice: want to do what is right; Think about where you came from
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what pursuing righteousness means and what the call to look at the rock is for.

records.heading: Look to the rock you were cut from

records.source: הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֣ם אֲבִיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־שָׂרָ֖ה תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶ֑ם כִּי־אֶחָ֣ד קְרָאתִ֔יו וַאֲבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וְאַרְבֵּֽהוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah [who] bore you; for one I called him, and I blessed him and I multiplied him.
pieces: Look to Abraham your ancestor \q and to Sarah, who gave birth to your people. \q When I called him he was a single man, \q yet I blessed him and made him many.

L.2: Look to Abraham your father \q and to Sarah [who] bore you; \q for [when he was but] one I called him, \q and I blessed him and multiplied him.

R.2: Think about Abraham, your ancestor, \q and Sarah, the mother of your nation. \q When I chose Abraham, he was only one man. \q But I blessed him and gave him many descendants.

decisions.choice: one I called, blessed and multiplied: the promise to Abraham in Genesis
decisions.reason: God called Abraham alone and promised to bless him and make him many (Genesis 12:1-3; 15:5; 22:17). Ezekiel 33:24 uses the same argument. If God made a nation from one man, he can rebuild the few left after the exile.

decisions.choice: your father, who bore you: the founding ancestors of the nation
decisions.reason: Abraham is "father" as ancestor; Sarah "bore you" as mother of the people through Isaac.

decisions.choice: your ancestor; gave birth to your people / the mother of your nation
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Abraham and Sarah are the parents of the nation, not of each hearer.

records.source: כִּֽי־נִחַ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה צִיּ֗וֹן נִחַם֙ כָּל־חָרְבֹתֶ֔יהָ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם מִדְבָּרָהּ֙ כְּעֵ֔דֶן וְעַרְבָתָ֖הּ כְּגַן־יְהוָ֑ה שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא בָ֔הּ תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֥וֹל זִמְרָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For Yahweh will comfort Zion, he will comfort all her waste places, and he made her wilderness like Eden and her desert like [the] garden of Yahweh; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and [the] sound of music.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring comfort to all her ruined places. \q He will make her wilderness like Eden, \q her barren plain like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Gladness and delight will be found in her, \q songs of thanks and the sound of music.

L.3: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will comfort all her ruins, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make her wilderness like Eden \q and her desert like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q joy and gladness will be found in her, \q thanksgiving and the sound of song.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort the people of Zion. He will comfort them in all the places that lie in ruins. \q He will make their dry land like the garden of Eden, \q like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People there will be happy and glad. \q They will sing songs and thank God.

decisions.choice: will comfort, will make: the past-tense verbs describe what is certain to come
decisions.reason: The verbs are perfect forms, but the context looks forward: the prophet speaks of the coming restoration as if it were already done. The same certainty marks 40:1 and 52:9.

decisions.choice: like Eden, like the garden of the LORD: the first garden restored
decisions.reason: Eden is the garden God planted (Genesis 2:8-15; 13:10; Ezekiel 36:35). The ruined land will be made as fruitful and full of life as the first garden.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion; their dry land
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that comforting Zion means comforting her people, and joins the two parallel pictures of wilderness and desert.

records.source: הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: Pay attention to me, my people, and my nation, to me give ear; for instruction from me will go out, and my justice to a light of peoples I will set at rest.
pieces: Listen closely to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; \q hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation. \q Instruction will go out from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice stand firm as a light for the peoples.

L.4: Pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation, give ear to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q for instruction will go out from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice I will set as a light for [the] peoples.

R.4: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q Pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation. \q I will give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching, and it will go out to the world. \q I will set up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice, and it will be a light for all nations.

decisions.choice: instruction will go out, a light for the peoples: God's teaching and justice reaching all nations
decisions.reason: The words echo 2:3, where instruction goes out from Zion to the nations, and 42:4, 6 and 49:6, where the servant brings justice and is a light to the nations.

decisions.choice: I will set at rest: I will establish it firmly
decisions.reason: The verb means to give rest or settle (Jeremiah 31:2). The same root is also used of something done in a moment (Jeremiah 49:19), and some read it as "in a moment", joined to verse 5: "In a moment my righteousness is near."

decisions.choice: it will go out to the world; all nations
decisions.reason: Readable says where the teaching goes, as the parallel line about the peoples implies.

records.source: קָר֤וֹב צִדְקִי֙ יָצָ֣א יִשְׁעִ֔י וּזְרֹעַ֖י עַמִּ֣ים יִשְׁפֹּ֑טוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֣ים יְקַוּ֔וּ וְאֶל־זְרֹעִ֖י יְיַחֵלֽוּן׃
records.gloss: Near [is] my righteousness, has gone out my salvation, and my arms peoples will judge; to me islands will wait, and to my arm they will wait.
pieces: My righteousness is close; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation has set out, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arms will judge the peoples. \q The coastlands look to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in hope, \q and they wait for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm.

L.5: Near [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation has gone out, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arms will judge [the] peoples; \q the coastlands will wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm they will hope.

R.5: I will soon set things right. I am already on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way to save. \q With {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power I will judge the nations. \q Lands far away are waiting for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They hope I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power for them.

decisions.choice: my righteousness: God's saving justice, his setting things right
decisions.reason: Set beside "my salvation", righteousness here is God acting to put right what is wrong and to rescue his people, as in 46:13 and 56:1.

decisions.choice: my arms, my arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength used for a task (40:10; 52:10; 53:1). The arms that judge also save: the coastlands wait for that arm in hope.

decisions.choice: will judge the peoples: rule them with justice
decisions.reason: To judge here is to govern and set right, not only to condemn (2:4; Psalm 96:13).

decisions.choice: I will soon set things right; I am on my way to save; with my power
decisions.reason: Readable turns the nouns into what God does and explains the arm as power.

records.source: שְׂאוּ֩ לַשָּׁמַ֨יִם עֵֽינֵיכֶ֜ם וְֽהַבִּ֧יטוּ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ מִתַּ֗חַת כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֜יִם כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן נִמְלָ֨חוּ֙ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד תִּבְלֶ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כְּמוֹ־כֵ֣ן יְמוּת֑וּן וִישֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לֹ֥א תֵחָֽת׃ס
records.gloss: Lift up to the heavens your eyes, and look to the earth from beneath; for [the] heavens like smoke will be dispersed, and the earth like a garment will wear out, and its inhabitants like gnat[s] will die; and my salvation forever will be, and my righteousness not will be shattered.
pieces: Raise your eyes to the sky and look at the earth below. \q The sky will drift away like smoke, the earth will fray like old clothing, \q and those who live on it will die like gnats. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will remain forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will never give way.

L.6: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look to the earth beneath; \q for the heavens will vanish like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, \q and its inhabitants will die like gnats; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will be forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will not be shattered.

R.6: Look up at the sky, and look down at the earth. The sky will disappear like smoke. The earth will wear out like old clothes. \q The people who live on it will die like tiny insects. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will last forever. \q My power to set things right will never fail.

decisions.choice: like gnats: like tiny insects that die in swarms
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read as one word meaning "in the same way", or as "like a gnat", from a word for small insects (compare Exodus 8:12-14). The second gives a picture that fits the smoke and the garment.

decisions.choice: the heavens and earth pass away, but God's salvation lasts forever
decisions.reason: Even the created world is temporary compared with what God does to save (Psalm 102:26-28; Hebrews 1:10-12). Isaiah also speaks of new heavens and a new earth (65:17; 66:22).

decisions.choice: My power to set things right will never fail
decisions.reason: Readable explains God's righteousness here as his setting things right, as in verse 5.

records.source: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל־תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל־תֵּחָֽתּוּ׃
records.gloss: Listen to me, knowers of righteousness, a people [with] my instruction in their heart; do not fear [the] reproach of humankind, and from their revilings do not be dismayed.
pieces: Hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who know what is right, \q you people who carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction in your hearts: \q do not be afraid when mortals mock you, \q and do not lose heart at their abuse.

L.7: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [you] who know righteousness, \q [the] people [with] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction in their heart: \q do not fear [the] scorn of mortals, \q and do not be shattered by their insults.

R.7: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who know what is right. \q You keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching in your hearts. \q Do not be afraid when people make fun of you. \q Do not be upset when they insult you.

decisions.choice: my instruction in their heart: God's teaching taken in and loved
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 6:6 and Psalm 37:31 speak of God's instruction on the heart; Jeremiah 31:33 promises a covenant in which God writes it there.

decisions.choice: mortals: human beings as weak and passing
decisions.reason: The word for humankind here stresses frailty. Verse 8 shows why their scorn need not be feared: they will be eaten like cloth (compare verse 12).

decisions.choice: know what is right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express knowing righteousness as knowing what is right, since the line speaks of the people's way of life.

records.source: כִּ֤י כַבֶּ֨גֶד֙ יֹאכְלֵ֣ם עָ֔שׁ וְכַצֶּ֖מֶר יֹאכְלֵ֣ם סָ֑ס וְצִדְקָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וִישׁוּעָתִ֖י לְד֥וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: For like a garment a moth will eat them, and like wool a clothes-moth will eat them; and my righteousness forever will be, and my salvation to a generation of generations.
pieces: Like clothing, they will be eaten by moths; \q like wool, they will be chewed by grubs. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will stand forever, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation through every generation.

L.8: For like a garment the moth will eat them, \q and like wool the worm will eat them; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will be forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation to generation [after] generation.

R.8: Moths will eat them up like clothes. \q Worms will eat them like wool. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power to set things right will last forever. \q I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in every generation.

decisions.choice: moth, clothes-moth: insects whose larvae eat cloth
decisions.reason: The second word is a rarer term for the moth or its grub that eats wool. Both lines picture the mockers wasting away (50:9).

decisions.choice: my righteousness forever, my salvation to all generations
decisions.reason: Verse 6 closes the same way, with the two words in the other order. The repetition frames verses 6-8: what God does to save will outlast everything that opposes it.

decisions.choice: my power to set things right; I will save my people
decisions.reason: Readable explains righteousness as in verse 6 and turns salvation into what God does.

records.source: עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי־עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ־הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין׃
records.gloss: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Yahweh; awake as [in] days of antiquity, generations of ages; [are] you not she [who] cut in pieces Rahab, [who] pierced [the] sea monster?
pieces: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Awake as in days long gone, in ages past! \q Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who cut Rahab to pieces, \q who ran the sea monster through?

L.9: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Awake as [in] days of old, [the] generations of long ago! \q [Was it] not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who hacked Rahab in pieces, \q who pierced the sea monster?

R.9: Wake up! Wake up, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Put on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength! \q Wake up as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did long ago, in the days of our ancestors. \q Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who cut Rahab into pieces? \q You stabbed that sea monster.

decisions.choice: awake, arm of the LORD: a cry to God to act with his power, as if he were asleep
decisions.reason: The people call on the LORD's arm, his power in action (verse 5; 53:1), as one wakes a sleeper (Psalm 44:24). The arm is God himself acting, so the words addressed to it are words to God. Later God turns the cry back on Jerusalem: "Rouse yourself" (verse 17; 52:1).

decisions.choice: Rahab, the sea monster: the monster of the sea, and a name for Egypt
decisions.reason: Rahab is a sea monster whom God defeats (Job 26:12; Psalm 89:11), and the same name is used for Egypt (30:7; Psalm 87:4). The sea monster is also named in 27:1. Verse 10 shows the sense: God's victory over the sea at the exodus was a victory over Egypt. The name is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: as in days of old: as God acted at the exodus
decisions.reason: The prayer asks God to act again as he did when he brought Israel out of Egypt (63:11-13; Psalm 77:6, 12-21).

decisions.choice: in the days of our ancestors; that sea monster
decisions.reason: Readable explains "generations of long ago" and links the monster to Rahab.

records.heading: Awake, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: הֲל֤וֹא אַתְּ־הִיא֙ הַמַּחֲרֶ֣בֶת יָ֔ם מֵ֖י תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֑ה הַשָּׂ֨מָה֙ מַֽעֲמַקֵּי־יָ֔ם דֶּ֖רֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֥ר גְּאוּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: [Are] you not she [who] dried up [the] sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of [the] sea a way to pass over [for the] redeemed?
pieces: Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who drained the sea, \q the waters of the vast deep, \q and turned the sea's depths into a road for the redeemed to cross?

L.10: [Was it] not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who dried up the sea, \q the waters of the great deep, \q who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross?

R.10: Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who dried up the sea and the deep waters? \q You made a road through the bottom of the sea, \q so that the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought back could walk across.

decisions.choice: dried up the sea, a way for the redeemed to cross: the crossing of the sea in the exodus
decisions.reason: God dried up the sea and his people walked through it (Exodus 14:21-22, 29; 15:13, 16). The great deep recalls the waters of creation and the flood (Genesis 1:2; 7:11).

decisions.choice: the redeemed: those God bought back, as a kinsman frees a relative
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's redeeming Israel from Egypt (Exodus 6:6; 15:13) and of the return from Babylon (35:9; 43:1).

decisions.choice: the people you bought back
decisions.reason: Readable explains "redeemed" with the settled wording for this verb.

records.source: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשׁוּב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂיג֔וּן נָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And the ransomed of Yahweh will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting gladness [will be] upon their head; joy and gladness will overtake [them]; sorrow and sighing will flee.
pieces: Those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has ransomed will come back; they will enter Zion with glad shouts, \q with joy that never ends resting on their heads. \q Delight and gladness will catch up with them, \q and grief and groaning will run away.

L.11: And [the] ransomed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, \q and everlasting joy [will be] upon their heads; \q gladness and joy will overtake [them], \q [and] sorrow and sighing will flee.

R.11: The people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set free will come home. They will enter Zion singing and shouting. \q Their joy will last forever, and everyone will see it on them. \q Happiness and joy will catch up with them. \q Sadness and crying will run away.

decisions.choice: the ransomed of the LORD will return: the same words as 35:10
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 35:10 almost word for word (see the notes there on "ransomed", the joy on their heads and the joy that overtakes them). After the memory of the exodus in verse 10, the return from exile is pictured as a new exodus.

decisions.choice: sorrow and sighing will flee: the verb has no "and" before it here
decisions.reason: In 35:10 the last line begins with "and"; here it does not. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Those the LORD has ransomed / The people the LORD has set free
decisions.reason: The wording follows 35:10, which has the same Hebrew.

records.source: אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם מִֽי־אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמ֔וּת וּמִבֶּן־אָדָ֖ם חָצִ֥יר יִנָּתֵֽן׃
records.gloss: I, I [am] he [who] comforts you; who [are] you, and you have been afraid of a person [who] dies, and of a son of humankind [who] is made [like] grass?
pieces: I, I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who comforts you. \q Who are you, to be afraid of mortals who die, \q of human beings who wither like grass,

L.12: I, I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who comforts you. \q Who [are] you, that you are afraid of a man [who] dies, \q and of a son of man [who] is made [like] grass,

R.12: I myself am the one who comforts you. \q So why are you afraid of people? \q They are only human. They will die and dry up like grass.

decisions.choice: I, I am he who comforts you: God alone is the comforter of his people
decisions.reason: The doubled "I" with "he" echoes the claim "I am he" (see the note at 43:10; 43:25). Here it is joined to comfort, picking up 40:1 and verse 3.

decisions.choice: a son of man made like grass: a mortal, who withers and dies
decisions.reason: "Son of man" means a human being. Grass that dries up pictures how short human life is (40:6-8; Psalm 103:15-16).

decisions.choice: who are you: the question is to Zion, and runs on into verse 13
decisions.reason: "You" is feminine here, Zion as a woman; in verse 13 it turns masculine, the people. The question asks how they can fear mortals and forget their Maker.

decisions.choice: I myself am the one who comforts you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the stress of the doubled "I" in plain words; this is not the absolute "I am he" of 43:10, so the wording "I alone am God" is not used here.

decisions.choice: a man ... a son of man / mortals ... human beings
decisions.reason: The two words mean human beings, men and women alike. Balanced uses inclusive words; Literal keeps the form "son of man" so the reader can see the idiom.

records.source: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֞ח יְהוָ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ נוֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַיִם֮ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָרֶץ֒ וַתְּפַחֵ֨ד תָּמִ֜יד כָּל־הַיּ֗וֹם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֵּצִ֔יק כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר כּוֹנֵ֖ן לְהַשְׁחִ֑ית וְאַיֵּ֖ה חֲמַ֥ת הַמֵּצִֽיק׃
records.gloss: and you have forgotten Yahweh [who] made you, [who] stretched out [the] heavens and founded [the] earth, and you have been in dread continually all the day from before the fury of the oppressor, when he has prepared to destroy? And where [is] the fury of the oppressor?
pieces: and you have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Maker, who spread out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth? \q Day after day you live in constant dread of the oppressor's rage \q as he takes aim to destroy. \q But where is the oppressor's rage now?

L.13: and you have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Maker, [who] stretched out [the] heavens and founded [the] earth, \q and you dread continually all day long the fury of the oppressor, \q as he makes ready to destroy? \q And where [is] the fury of the oppressor?

R.13: You have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who made you. He spread out the sky and made the earth firm. \q But all day long you are terrified of the angry person who is crushing you \q and getting ready to destroy you. \q Where is that anger now? It is gone!

decisions.choice: you have forgotten the LORD your Maker: fear of people comes from forgetting the Creator
decisions.reason: The one who made Israel also stretched out the sky and founded the earth (40:22; 42:5; 44:24). To fear a mortal oppressor is to forget how great he is.

decisions.choice: the oppressor: the power that holds the people captive, Babylon
decisions.reason: The word means one who presses hard or hems in. In these chapters the captor is Babylon (47:6; verse 14).

decisions.choice: where is the fury of the oppressor: a question that expects the answer that it is gone
decisions.reason: The question mocks the oppressor's rage as already past (compare 33:18). Verse 14 says the captive will soon be set free.

decisions.choice: It is gone!
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question implies.

records.source: מִהַ֥ר צֹעֶ֖ה לְהִפָּתֵ֑חַ וְלֹא־יָמ֣וּת לַשַּׁ֔חַת וְלֹ֥א יֶחְסַ֖ר לַחְמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He will hasten, [one who is] stooping, to be released, and not he will die to the pit, and not he will lack his bread.
pieces: The one bent low in chains will soon be released; \q he will not die and go down to the pit, \q nor will he go without bread.

L.14: The one bowed down will hasten to be set free, \q and he will not die [and go down] to the pit, \q and he will not lack his bread.

R.14: Soon the prisoners will be set free. \q They will not die in prison or be buried in a grave. \q They will have enough food to eat.

decisions.choice: one bowed down: a captive bent under chains or in a cramped cell
decisions.reason: The word describes one stooping or bent low (63:1 uses it of one bending under his load). The context of the oppressor in verse 13 shows it is the prisoner of the exile (42:7, 22).

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, or a pit used as a prison
decisions.reason: The word is used of the grave and the place of the dead (38:17; Psalm 16:10). A dry cistern could also serve as a prison (Jeremiah 38:6), so both senses may be in view.

decisions.choice: the prisoners; die in prison or be buried in a grave
decisions.reason: Readable explains the one bowed down as the prisoners, and gives both sides of the word for the pit.

records.source: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ רֹגַ֣ע הַיָּ֔ם וַיֶּהֱמ֖וּ גַּלָּ֑יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I [am] Yahweh your God, [who] stirs up the sea and its waves roar; Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.
pieces: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who stirs up the sea until its waves roar; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.15: And I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

R.15: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. \q I stir up the sea and make its waves roar. \q My name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: stirs up: churns the sea into a storm
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to stir up or to calm. The roaring waves that follow favor "stir up". Jeremiah 31:35 has the same line, and Job 26:12 uses the verb of God's power over the sea alongside Rahab.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts: the LORD who commands the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: See the note at 1:9.

decisions.choice: My name is the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself in the third person ("his name"). Readable puts it in the first person, as the rest of the verse is.

records.source: וָאָשִׂ֤ים דְּבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יךָ וּבְצֵ֥ל יָדִ֖י כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ לִנְטֹ֤עַ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלִיסֹ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְלֵאמֹ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן עַמִּי־אָֽתָּה׃ס
records.gloss: And I have put my words in your mouth, and with the shadow of my hand I have covered you, to plant [the] heavens and to found [the] earth, and to say to Zion, my people [are] you.
pieces: I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth \q and sheltered you in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, \q to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, \q and to say to Zion, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."

L.16: And I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth, \q and in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand I have covered you, \q to plant [the] heavens and to found [the] earth, \q and to say to Zion, "You [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."

R.16: I have given you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to speak. \q I have kept you safe, as if I were shading you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand. \q I did this so that I could set the sky in place, make the earth firm, \q and say to the people of Zion, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."

decisions.choice: your mouth, covered you: the one addressed is Israel, or God's spokesman, the servant
decisions.reason: The same words are said of the servant in 49:2 ("in the shadow of his hand he hid me") and of the prophet's words in 59:21. Here "you" is masculine and is told it will say to Zion "You are my people", so it may be the servant or the prophet rather than the whole people.

decisions.choice: to plant the heavens: to set the heavens firmly in place
decisions.reason: The verb normally means to plant (a tree) or pitch (a tent). It is used here beside "found the earth"; verse 13 has "stretched out" the heavens instead. The planting may point to a new creation (65:17).

decisions.choice: you are my people: the covenant words
decisions.reason: These are the words of the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Hosea 2:25). The exile seemed to say "not my people" (Hosea 1:9); God now says the opposite.

decisions.choice: as if I were shading you; I did this so that
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand's shadow and spells out the purpose clause.

records.source: הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י ק֚וּמִי יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁתִ֛ית מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־כּ֣וֹס חֲמָת֑וֹ אֶת־קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֛ה שָׁתִ֖ית מָצִֽית׃
records.gloss: Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, arise, Jerusalem, who have drunk from the hand of Yahweh the cup of his anger; the bowl of the cup of staggering you have drunk, you have drained.
pieces: Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, \q you who have drunk from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath, \q who have drunk the goblet that makes people reel and emptied it to the bottom.

L.17: Awake, awake, rise up, Jerusalem, \q you who have drunk from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath; \q the bowl, the cup of staggering, you have drunk [and] drained.

R.17: Wake up! Wake up! Get up, people of Jerusalem! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with you and punished you. It was as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you drink a cup full of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q You drank every drop, and it made you stagger like someone who is drunk.

decisions.choice: the cup of his wrath, the cup of staggering: God's judgment pictured as a drink that makes one reel
decisions.reason: God's anger is a cup he gives to drink, and those who drink it stagger like drunkards (Jeremiah 25:15-29; Psalm 75:9; Ezekiel 23:31-34). Jerusalem has drunk it in the fall of the city and the exile. Revelation 14:10 and 16:19 use the same picture.

decisions.choice: rouse yourself, rouse yourself: the call of verse 9 turned back on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The people cried to the LORD's arm, "Awake, awake" (verse 9). Now God calls Jerusalem to wake up, with a form of the verb that means "rouse yourself". The same call comes again in 52:1.

decisions.choice: the bowl ... drained: drunk to the last drop
decisions.reason: The word for the bowl is a large cup or goblet, found only here and in verse 22. "Drained" means wrung out to the dregs (Psalm 75:9).

decisions.choice: Awake, awake
decisions.reason: The verb differs from the one in verse 9, but it has the same sense, so the same words are used to show that God answers the people's cry with his own.

decisions.choice: The LORD was angry with you and punished you. It was as if
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for before giving the picture.

records.heading: The cup of wrath taken away

records.source: אֵין־מְנַהֵ֣ל לָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים יָלָ֑דָה וְאֵ֤ין מַחֲזִיק֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים גִּדֵּֽלָה׃
records.gloss: There is not [one] leading her from all [the] children she has borne, and there is not [one] taking hold of her hand from all [the] children she has brought up.
pieces: Of all the {{gender:children|sons}} she bore, there is not one to guide her; \q of all the {{gender:children|sons}} she raised, there is no one to take her by the hand.

L.18: There is no [one] to guide her among all the {{gender:children|sons}} she has borne, \q and there is no [one] to take her by the hand among all the {{gender:children|sons}} she has raised.

R.18: She had many children, but none of them is there to lead her home. \q She raised them, but not one of them takes her hand to help her walk.

decisions.choice: no one to guide her, no one to take her by the hand: no child helps the reeling mother
decisions.reason: A mother who staggers needs her children to hold her up and lead her home; it was a child's duty to care for a parent. Jerusalem's children are themselves fallen (verse 20), so she has no help.

decisions.choice: her: the address to Jerusalem turns briefly to the third person
decisions.reason: Verse 17 spoke to Jerusalem as "you"; verse 18 speaks about her, then verse 19 returns to "you".

records.source: שְׁתַּ֤יִם הֵ֨נָּה֙ קֹֽרְאֹתַ֔יִךְ מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ הַשֹּׁ֧ד וְהַשֶּׁ֛בֶר וְהָרָעָ֥ב וְהַחֶ֖רֶב מִ֥י אֲנַחֲמֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Two [things] these [have] befallen you; who will show sympathy to you? The devastation and the destruction, and the famine and the sword; who [as] I will comfort you?
pieces: These two disasters have come upon you; \q who will grieve for you? \q Devastation and ruin, famine and sword: how can I comfort you?

L.19: These two [things] have happened to you; \q who will grieve with you? \q Ruin and destruction, famine and sword; how will I comfort you?

R.19: Two kinds of trouble have come upon you. \q Your land was destroyed and ruined, and your people died from hunger and war. \q Who will feel sorry for you? How can I comfort you?

decisions.choice: two things, four words: two pairs, ruin of the land and death of the people
decisions.reason: "Two" is followed by four words in two pairs: devastation and destruction strike the city and land; famine and sword strike its people.

decisions.choice: how will I comfort you: the standard Hebrew text has the first person
decisions.reason: The standard text reads literally "who, I comfort you?", best taken as "how will I comfort you?" (compare Amos 7:2, 5). The Great Isaiah Scroll and the Septuagint (from memory; to be checked) have "who will comfort you?", matching the earlier question in the verse. The standard text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Your land was destroyed and ruined, and your people died from hunger and war
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two pairs and moves the first question after them.

records.source: בָּנַ֜יִךְ עֻלְּפ֥וּ שָׁכְב֛וּ בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־חוּצ֖וֹת כְּת֣וֹא מִכְמָ֑ר הַֽמְלֵאִ֥ים חֲמַת־יְהוָ֖ה גַּעֲרַ֥ת אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: Your children have fainted; they have lain at [the] head of all [the] streets like an antelope [in] a net, the [ones] full of the anger of Yahweh, the rebuke of your God.
pieces: Your {{gender:children|sons}} have collapsed; they lie at the corner of every street like an antelope in a net, \q filled to the brim with the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the rebuke of your God.

L.20: Your {{gender:children|sons}} have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope [caught in] a net, \q full of the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the rebuke of your God.

R.20: Your people have fainted. They lie at the corner of every street, like a wild animal caught in a net. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God was angry and punished them, and they could not take any more.

decisions.choice: antelope: a wild animal of the oryx or antelope kind
decisions.reason: The word is listed among clean wild animals in Deuteronomy 14:5. Caught in a hunter's net, it struggles until it is exhausted.

decisions.choice: full of the wrath of the LORD: they have drunk the cup of verse 17 to the full
decisions.reason: The cup picture continues: Jerusalem's children are filled with God's anger as with strong drink and lie helpless (Jeremiah 13:13; Lamentations 2:11-12, 19).

decisions.choice: Your people; a wild animal; could not take any more
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" for the city's children, describes the antelope, and explains "full of the wrath".

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי־נָ֥א זֹ֖את עֲנִיָּ֑ה וּשְׁכֻרַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א מִיָּֽיִן׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore hear, please, this, afflicted [one], and drunken [one], and not from wine.
pieces: So hear this, you who are afflicted, \q you who are drunk but not with wine:

L.21: Therefore hear this, afflicted [one], \q drunk, but not with wine:

R.21: So listen to this, you poor, suffering people. \q You stagger like someone who is drunk, but not from drinking wine.

decisions.choice: drunk, but not with wine: staggering from God's judgment, not from drink
decisions.reason: The cup of wrath (verse 17) has made Jerusalem reel. The same expression is used in 29:9.

decisions.choice: therefore hear this: the turn to the promise of verses 22-23
decisions.reason: Because no one else comforts her (verses 18-19), God himself now speaks to Jerusalem.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֨יִךְ֙ יָרִ֣יב עַמּ֔וֹ הִנֵּ֥ה לָקַ֛חְתִּי מִיָּדֵ֖ךְ אֶת־כּ֣וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֑ה אֶת־קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס חֲמָתִ֔י לֹא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Thus says your lord Yahweh, and your God [who] contends [for] his people: Here! I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, the bowl of the cup of my anger; not you will repeat to drink it again.
pieces: Your Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your God who takes up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people's cause, says this: \q See, I have taken out of your hand the cup that makes you reel. \q The goblet of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath you will never drink again.

L.22: Thus says your Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and your God, [who] pleads the cause of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: \q Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, \q the bowl, the cup of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath; \q you will not drink it again.

R.22: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Master says, your God who defends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: \q Look, I have taken away the cup that made you stagger. \q I have taken the cup of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger from you. \q You will never have to drink from it again.

decisions.choice: your Lord: your master, the one you serve
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form, as titles of majesty often are, and means lord or master. Used with the divine name it says the LORD is Jerusalem's rightful master (compare 1:24; 26:13).

decisions.choice: who pleads the cause of his people: who argues his people's case as their advocate
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing a case at law. Here God takes his people's side (Jeremiah 50:34; Psalm 43:1), as the servant's helper did in 50:8.

decisions.choice: I have taken the cup; you will not drink it again: the judgment on Jerusalem is over
decisions.reason: The cup of verse 17 is taken away for good (40:2; 54:9). Verse 23 says where it goes next.

decisions.choice: your Master
decisions.reason: Readable says "Master" for the title meaning lord, so that it is not confused with the divine name.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨יהָ֙ בְּיַד־מוֹגַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־אָמְר֥וּ לְנַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ שְׁחִ֣י וְנַעֲבֹ֑רָה וַתָּשִׂ֤ימִי כָאָ֨רֶץ֙ גֵּוֵ֔ךְ וְכַח֖וּץ לַעֹבְרִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And I will put it in [the] hand of [those who] grieve you, who said to your soul, Bow down, and let us pass over; and you made like the ground your back, and like the street for [those] passing over.
pieces: I will put it into the hands of those who tormented you, \q who said to you, "Lie face down, so we can walk across you." \q And you made your back like the ground, \q like a street for people to walk on.

L.23: And I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, \q who said to you, "Bow down, so that we may walk over [you]," \q and you made your back like the ground, \q and like the street for [those who] walk over [it].

R.23: Now I will make the people who hurt you drink from that cup. \q They told you, "Lie down on the ground so we can walk on you." \q And you had to let them. Your back became like a road for them to walk on.

decisions.choice: bow down so we may walk over you: conquerors treading on the backs of the defeated
decisions.reason: Victors in the ancient world sometimes made captives lie down and walked or rode over them, as a sign of complete defeat (Joshua 10:24; Psalm 66:12; 129:3).

decisions.choice: said to your soul: said to you
decisions.reason: "Your soul" here means "you yourself", as often in Hebrew. It may also suggest they spoke to crush her spirit.

decisions.choice: I will put it in the hand of your tormentors: the cup passes to the oppressors
decisions.reason: The judgment Jerusalem drank now goes to those who abused her (47:6; Jeremiah 25:15-17, 26).

decisions.choice: make the people who hurt you drink from that cup
decisions.reason: Readable says what putting the cup in their hand means.
